episodes.title: Why Does the Riemann Hypothesis Matter?
paragraphs: Why does the Riemann Hypothesis matter? I asked Claude the day after Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a proof of it, built with Claude, as 17 million lines of Lean code.

We start with Riemann himself and build up from nothing: why primes matter, Euclid’s proof that they never run out, Gauss’s estimate of how they thin out, and how the zeros of the zeta function turn that estimate into the exact count.
Then the proof: what’s known about how it works, which Millennium Prize problem could go next, and what mathematicians do with a result a machine can verify but no person can yet explain.

made: I recorded a conversation about the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude in voice mode, running Audio Hijack to split Claude and my mic, and QuickTime for video, which gave me three files: my voice audio, Claude’s voice, and a camera.
After recording, I pointed Claude Fable 5.2 at the folder, gave it a Render sandbox, and asked it to stitch together the audio files and add animations. No video editor!

It solved a lot of things that would have been super annoying (I am a Final Cut + Logic Pro user and could have fixed it by hand). But it found the camera’s sound ran 40 milliseconds behind my mic and shifted the mix so my lips match. I had recorded too loud and clipped my mic, so Claude wrote its own repair tool that guesses what each flattened peak should have looked like from the audio around it. Another crazy one was Claude’s voice was leaking into my mic, so it used its own clean recording to subtract itself. Then it took the room echo off my voice and matched our volumes.

I didn’t like some of Claude’s cheesy AI-tell lines, so it rebuilt sentences out of words it had actually said. Another cool moment is partway through recording I told Claude the RH proof had been announced after its training cutoff. It looked it up and was surprised.
